docs.title: NLP Well Report Analyzer
docs.text: Information extraction from unstructured drilling and completion reports.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This machine learning system is part of the Oil & Gas ML Portfolio by Kelvin J Cabrera.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Synthetic Data Generator -> Scikit-Learn Training -> Flask API -> Streamlit Dashboard

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Data Generation: Domain-aware synthetic data with physical correlations
  • Model Training: Scikit-learn pipelines (Random Forest, Isolation Forest) with MLflow tracking
  • API: Flask/FastAPI with API key authentication
  • Dashboard: Streamlit interactive web interface
  • Testing: pytest with model evaluation metrics (R2, accuracy, F1)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
pip install -r requirements.txt
python train.py
python app.py
streamlit run streamlit_app.py

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Endpoint Description GET / Service info and available models POST /predict/{model} Run inference (requires API key)

Authentication

All API endpoints require an X-API-Key header. Set API_KEY in your environment.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All API requests require an API key sent via the X-API-Key header.

import requests

headers = {"X-API-Key": "your-api-key"}
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5000/predict/model", json={...}, headers=headers)

docs.title: GET /
docs.text:
Returns service information and available models.

Response:

{"service": "NLP Well Report Analyzer", "models": ["model1", "model2"]}

docs.title: POST /predict/{model_name}
docs.text:
Run inference on a trained model.

Request Body:

{"features": {"feature_1": 0.5, "feature_2": 1.2}}

Response:

{"prediction": 0.85, "model": "model_name"}

docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text: Code Description 401 Invalid or missing API key 404 Model not found 422 Invalid input format

docs.title: Data Layer
docs.text:
• Data Generator: Creates synthetic well reports with realistic oil & gas terminology
  • Report Types: drilling, completion, workover, production (150 each, 600 total)
  • Content: Includes well names, depths, formations, equipment references
  • Sentiment Labels: Auto-labeled using keyword-based heuristics

docs.title: Report Classifier (ReportClassifier)
docs.text:
• Algorithm: Keyword-frequency-based classification
  • Approach: Matches report text against domain-specific term patterns for each report type
  • Scoring: Counts keyword occurrences per category, normalizes to probabilities
  • Categories: drilling, completion, workover, production
  • Persistence: Pickle (.pkl) at outputs/models/classifier.pkl

docs.title: Entity Extractor (EntityExtractor)
docs.text:
• Algorithm: Rule-based extraction using regex patterns
  • Entity Types:
  • well_name: Matches patterns like Cantarell-X1, Santa Barbara-3
  • depths: Matches depth measurements (e.g., 12500 feet, 8200-8500 ft)
  • formation: Matches geological formation names
  • equipment: Matches oil & gas equipment references (ESP, BOP, etc.)
  • Training: Builds frequency dictionaries from training corpus
  • Persistence: Pickle (.pkl) at outputs/models/entity_extractor.pkl

docs.title: Sentiment Analyzer (SentimentAnalyzer)
docs.text:
• Algorithm: Lexicon-based sentiment scoring
  • Approach: Uses industry-specific positive and negative indicator words
  • Positive Keywords: successful, excellent, good, improved, completed, optimized, achieved
  • Negative Keywords: failed, failure, problem, damage, loss, lost, stuck, severe, critical, incident
  • Scoring: Weighted sum of positive/negative word counts
  • Labels: positive, negative, neutral
  • Persistence: Pickle (.pkl) at outputs/models/sentiment.pkl

docs.title: Text Processor Utilities
docs.text:
• Tokenization: Custom word tokenizer with lowercase normalization
  • TF-IDF: Term frequency-inverse document frequency computation
  • Keyword Extraction: TF-IDF weighted term extraction

docs.title: API Layer
docs.text:
• Framework: Flask (Python)
  • Serialization: JSON request/response
  • Model Loading: Pickle deserialization at startup
  • Port: 5017

docs.title: Dashboard Layer
docs.text:
• Frontend: HTML/CSS/JavaScript (single page)
  • Visualization: Chart.js for classification probabilities and sentiment
  • Style: Dark-themed responsive UI

docs.title: Full Analysis Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Input Report Text
   ↓
2. Text Processor (tokenize, normalize)
   ↓
3. Parallel Analysis
   ├── Report Classifier → report type + probabilities
   ├── Entity Extractor → well names, depths, formations, equipment
   ├── Sentiment Analyzer → label + score
   └── Keyword Extractor → TF-IDF keywords
   ↓
4. Combined JSON Response
   ↓
5. Dashboard Display

docs.title: Classification Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Input Text
   ↓
2. Tokenization + Normalization
   ↓
3. Keyword Pattern Matching (per category)
   ↓
4. Score Normalization
   ↓
5. Report Type + Probabilities

docs.title: Entity Extraction Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Input Text
   ↓
2. Regex Pattern Matching
   ├── Well Name Patterns
   ├── Depth Measurement Patterns
   ├── Formation Name Patterns
   └── Equipment Name Patterns
   ↓
3. Extracted Entities

docs.title: Deployment Guide - NLP Well Report Analyzer
Build the Image
docs.text:
cd nlp-well-report-analyzer
docker build -t nlp-well-report-analyzer .

docs.title: Run the Container
docs.text: docker run -p 5017:5017 nlp-well-report-analyzer

docs.title: With Model Training
docs.text: docker run -p 5017:5017 nlp-well-report-analyzer bash -c "python train.py && python app.py"

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
version: '3.8'
services:
  nlp-analyzer:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "5017:5017"
    volumes:
      - ./outputs:/app/outputs
    environment:
      - FLASK_ENV=production
      - PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
    restart: unless-stopped

docs.text: Variable Description Default FLASK_ENV Flask environment mode development PYTHONUNBUFFERED Disable Python output buffering 1 PORT Server port (hardcoded in app.py) 5017

docs.title: Production Considerations
docs.text:
• Use gunicorn with multiple workers for production deployments
  • Set debug=True to debug=False in app.py for production
  • Configure proper logging for request/error tracking
  • Place behind a reverse proxy (nginx/Apache) for SSL termination
  • Models auto-load from outputs/models/ at startup
  • Pre-train models with train.py before starting the server
  • Lightweight dependencies - no heavy NLP libraries needed

docs.title: User Guide - NLP Well Report Analyzer
Overview
docs.text: The NLP Well Report Analyzer is a natural language processing system for automatically classifying, analyzing, and extracting information from oil and gas well reports. It processes drilling, completion, workover, and production reports using lightweight custom NLP implementations.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.8+
  • pip

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
cd nlp-well-report-analyzer
pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Train Models
docs.text:
python train.py

Generates 600 synthetic well reports and trains all three models. Models are saved to outputs/models/.

docs.title: Start the API Server
docs.text:
python app.py

The server starts on http://localhost:5017.

docs.title: Open the Dashboard
docs.text: Navigate to http://localhost:5017 in your browser.

docs.title: Run Tests
docs.text: python test_api.py

docs.title: Dashboard Features
docs.text:
• Full Analysis: Paste a well report to get classification, entities, sentiment, and keywords
  • Report Classification: Categorize reports into drilling, completion, workover, or production
  • Entity Extraction: Extract well names, depths, formations, and equipment
  • Sentiment Analysis: Determine report tone (positive, negative, neutral)
  • Keyword Extraction: Identify key terms using TF-IDF scoring

docs.title: Report Types
docs.text: Type Description Key Indicators drilling Drilling operations reports drill, bit, mud, casing, depth, wellbore completion Well completion reports perforated, completion, liner, cemented workover Workover/intervention reports workover, repairs, replaced, pulled production Production operations reports production, barrels, oil rate, water cut

docs.title: Using curl
docs.text:
Full analysis:

curl -X POST http://localhost:5017/api/analyze \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text": "Drilling report for well Cantarell-X1. Total depth reached 12500 feet in the Cretaceous formation."}'

Classify report type:

curl -X POST http://localhost:5017/api/classify \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text": "Workover operations performed on well Santa Barbara-3."}'

Extract entities:

curl -X POST http://localhost:5017/api/extract \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text": "ESP installed on well Ku-Maloob-Zaap-5 at 8200 feet depth."}'

docs.title: Using Python
docs.text:
import requests

text = "Drilling report for well Cantarell-X1. Total depth reached 12500 feet in the Cretaceous formation."

# Full analysis
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5017/api/analyze", json={"text": text})
result = response.json()
print(f"Type: {result['classification']['type']}")
print(f"Sentiment: {result['sentiment']['label']}")
print(f"Keywords: {result['keywords'][:5]}")

# Extract entities
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5017/api/extract", json={"text": text})
entities = response.json()["entities"]
for well in entities["well_names"]:
    print(f"Well: {well}")
for depth in entities["depths"]:
    print(f"Depth: {depth}")

docs.title: Using JavaScript
docs.text:
const response = await fetch("http://localhost:5017/api/analyze", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ text: "Your well report text here..." })
});
const data = await response.json();
console.log(`Type: ${data.classification.type}`);
console.log(`Sentiment: ${data.sentiment.label}`);

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: No heavy NLP libraries required - the system uses lightweight custom implementations built with Python standard library (math, re, json, collections, pickle).

docs.title: Training Pipeline
docs.text:
The training pipeline follows these steps:

  1. Data Generation: data_generator.py creates synthetic data with domain-specific physical correlations
  2. Preprocessing: Feature scaling via StandardScaler
  3. Training: Random Forest or Isolation Forest via scikit-learn
  4. Evaluation: R2 score, accuracy, classification report
  5. Logging: MLflow tracks parameters, metrics, and artifacts
  6. Serialization: Model + scaler + metadata saved as .pkl via joblib

docs.title: Model Files
docs.text:
Models are stored in outputs/models/*.pkl as dictionaries with:

Key Description model Trained scikit-learn estimator scaler Fitted StandardScaler feature_names List of input feature names target_name Target variable name metrics Evaluation metrics from training

docs.title: Retraining
docs.text:
To retrain:

python train.py

This will update the model files in outputs/models/ and log results to MLflow.
